newsitem.title: MOROCCO: U.N. envoy meets Moroccan party leaders on W.Sahara.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy meets Moroccan party leaders on W.Sahara.

text.p: U.N. envoy for Western Sahara James Baker met Moroccan political leaders on Thursday to discuss a U.N. peace plan for the disputed territory, a Moroccan party spokesman said.
"U.N. envoy James Baker listened to political leaders' opinion and comment, including the opposition led by the old-guard nationalist Istiqlal party," the spokesman said.

The former U.S. Secretary of State was appointed by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last month to try to resolve the dispute over the former Spanish colony. It is claimed by Morocco while the Algerian-backed Polisario Front seeks independence there.
The meeting with Baker, which lasted for more than an hour, aimed to explain "how important the (Western) Sahara issue is for the Moroccan people," the spokesman said.
The leaders represent the 10 political parties which have seats in the 333-parliament, he said.
Baker, who arrived in Rabat on Wednesday, told reporters his visit was a "fact-finding trip" on the disputed territory.
He held a working session with King Hassan II on Wednesday night on the U.N. peace plan in the (Western) Sahara and latest developments in the region, officials said.

A ceasefire in the Wester Sahara, monitored by a U.N. force, has held since September 1991. But plans for a U.N. referendum on the future of the territory have been stalled since January 1992 over who is eligible to vote.
The U.N. envoy, touring North Africa in a Spanish military airplane, will leave Morocco for Algiers on Friday.
